Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content: "373 :     public Vector3D negate() {\n374 :         return new Vector3D(-x, -y, -z);\n375 :     }"

Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- What the test expects:
  - It builds a 3D line from two far-apart points, then computes expected = line.getDirection().negate().
  - It calls Line.revert() and asserts the reverted line’s direction equals exactly the negation of the original direction (zero tolerance).

- Relevant implementation:
  - Line.revert():
    - Code: 
      public Line revert() {
          final Line reverted = new Line(zero, zero.subtract(direction));
          return reverted;
      }
    - This reconstructs a new Line from two points: p1 = zero and p2 = zero − direction.
  - Line.reset(p1, p2) (used by the constructor):
    - Code:
      final Vector3D delta = p2.subtract(p1);
      final double norm2 = delta.getNormSq();
      this.direction = new Vector3D(1.0 / FastMath.sqrt(norm2), delta);
    - So the direction for the new line is obtained by normalizing delta (which is −direction from the original line).

- Why this fails:
  - The original direction stored in the line is already a normalized vector computed with finite-precision arithmetic in reset (it’s very close to unit length but not exactly 1.0).
  - In revert(), delta = −direction (from that existing approximate unit vector). When reset() runs again, it recomputes norm2 = delta.getNormSq() and then applies another scaling by 1/sqrt(norm2).
  - Because norm2 is not exactly 1 due to rounding, the new normalization changes the vector slightly (not just a sign flip). Thus reverted.getDirection() is not bit-for-bit equal to line.getDirection().negate().
  - The test uses Assert.assertArrayEquals(..., 0) which requires exact equality, so even tiny deviations cause failure.

- Relation to the issue report:
  - The report states c0.m0() is imprecise and suggests using Vector3D.negate() for the direction. Here, c0.m0() corresponds to Line.revert().
  - The current revert() recreates and renormalizes the direction, losing precision (~10 digits noted in the report) especially noticeable for lines defined by large coordinates.
  - A precise fix is to avoid recomputing/renormalizing the direction and simply negate the existing direction vector (Vector3D.negate()), which preserves the original components exactly up to the sign and makes the test pass.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
